newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks led up by brewing.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks led up by brewing.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended up led by brewing giant Bavaria and amid heavy demand for insurance firm Suramericana, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index gained 0.71 percent to close at 1,191.55 amid a 3 billion peso trade. Medellin's IBOMED general price index was up 0.64 percent to 18,131.67. An estimate of volume in Medellin was unavailable due to technical problems.
Bavaria, flagship of the Santo Domingo industrial empire, climbed 2.93 percent to 8,060 and 2.4 percent to the same price in Medellin.
"The market was fairly busy and was driven mostly by Bavaria and Suramericana...there are high expectations for the first half results of both companies," one Bogota broker said.
Demand came from both foreign funds and local investors on the first day of trading this week, following Monday's bank holiday for St Peter and St Paul's day.
Suramericana, flagship of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, remained unchanged at 28,200 amid a 1.75 billion peso volume in Bogota and a 2.7 billion peso volume in Medellin.
Foreign funds drove demand for Colombia's largest food manufacturer Compania Nacional de Chocolates. It gained 0.51 percent to 9,750 on the Medellin exchange.
